thread:
maya: Heads up — since the 03:00 deploy we saw ~20 ALB target deregistrations in eu-west-1 for edge-pool-ssd. All show readiness probe timeout (HTTP 504 from kube-proxy). Pods themselves report healthy locally :confused:
ashwin: Any config change to readiness/liveness or egress rules?
maya: no changes to readiness. readiness probe is standard /ready 1s timeout, 3 failures. This looks network-y — ALB healthchecks time out, then targets go Draining.
sre-oncall: Can you paste the pod readiness probe config + recent kube-proxy/kubelet logs? Also check conntrack counters on node when it happens: `cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count` and `nf_conntrack_max`.
maya: pasted snippets:
```
# readiness config
readinessProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /ready
    port: 8080
  initialDelaySeconds: 5
  periodSeconds: 10
  timeoutSeconds: 1
  failureThreshold: 3
```
`kubectl get pods -o wide --selector=app=edge -n inference` shows pods Ready=1/1 before ALB removal, then quickly 0/1 when ALB sees timeout.
naomi: deploy-bot shows the rollout succeeded: `deploy-bot: rollout complete for edge-service/v2 at 02:58 UTC` — timing matches. Could be burst of outbound connections during startup causing SNAT port exhaustion.
ashwin: do we NAT node egress through a small pool? Check `iptables -t nat -L -n -v` and `sudo conntrack -S | grep "tcp"` — look for massive TIME_WAIT or ephemeral port reuse.
maya: got these from one node during spike:
```
# conntrack summary
tcp            123456
udp            3456
expect         0
# /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max
65536
```
and `ss -s` shows a huge number of TIME_WAIT sockets.
sre-oncall: 65k max is low for our edge nodes under heavy bursting. When ephemeral ports / conntrack entries are exhausted, new outbound connections get dropped or reset which makes the healthcheck TCP handshake fail. ALB healthchecks are ephemeral but still need NAT ports when routed through SNAT gateway.
nashwin: two mitigation options: 1) increase nf_conntrack_max and ephemeral port range on nodes; 2) reduce SNAT pressure by moving healthchecks to not require SNAT — put ALB in same VPC and use target type=ip, or use target group healthcheck -> register targets by pod IP if using CNI with pod IPs reachable. Also consider a dedicated NAT instance with larger port range.
aomi: quick patch we can do now? Ops team wants a short-lived fix before business hours.
sre-oncall: quick steps: bump conntrack on nodes + restart kube-proxy only if needed. Commands: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144` and `sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range=\"15000 61000\"`. Then monitor `conntrack -S` and ALB target status. This avoids a full node reboot.
maya: doing `kubectl ssh node/x && sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144` on a canary node now.
(5m later)
maya: canary node bumped, conntrack count dropped below threshold, ALB stops deregistering for pods on that node. :thumbsup:
nashwin: long-term we should: add a cluster autoscaler hook to pre-warm connections, and plan to move edge pods onto instances with larger ephemeral port ranges / or add egress NAT gateways. Also evaluate AWS CNI config `ENIConfig` for more IPs per node so ALB can reach pod IPs directly.
sre-oncall: filing follow-up runbook: increase conntrack, monitor, and if recurrent escalate to networking to provision NAT gateway with more ports or change load balancer strategy.
aomi: noted, I'll open a ticket and schedule a postmortem with infra + networking.
deploy-bot: rollout-v2 -> 02:58 UTC (success), note: no image rollback performed.
maya: thanks all — rolling the conntrack bump to remaining nodes slowly, will report back in 30m.
